records.description_en: The A4S is an automated microplate heat sealer used in laboratories to apply sealing films to microplates under controlled temperature and time conditions. It is used with PCR plates, deep-well plates, or storage plates to create a secure seal for sample storage, evaporation and contamination control, and automated sample-processing workflows.

records.name_en: AA Opto MDS Acousto-Optic Tunable Filter
records.description_en: This is an AA Opto MDS-series acousto-optic tunable filter and controller used to control laser transmission, RF drive power, and operating frequency on individual channels, enabling fast wavelength selection and intensity modulation. It is commonly used in fluorescence microscopy, laser scanning, and multi-laser laboratory setups for rapid optical switching and beam control.

A multi-axis controller for microscope automation that can drive X, Y, and Z stage or focus axes, and on some configurations also control LED illumination channels. It is commonly used for sample positioning, scanning, focusing, and coordinated light control in microscopy experiments.

A benchtop multimode microplate reader used to measure absorbance, fluorescence, and luminescence from samples in microplates. It typically includes a plate tray, temperature control, and shaking, and is used for biochemical assays, cell-based experiments, and high-throughput screening.

An automated microplate centrifuge for laboratory workflows. It can load and unload plates, open and close the door, lock the bucket, and perform spin operations. It is commonly used for short spins, collecting droplets, and plate-level sample preparation in automated lab systems.

BITalino is a portable Bluetooth biosignal acquisition device with multiple analog input channels for collecting and streaming physiological or other low-frequency analog sensor signals in laboratory experiments. It is commonly used for teaching, prototyping, and wearable physiology measurements.

This is a non-physical software component that connects to a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) device, subscribes to its notifications, organizes incoming samples into chunks, and publishes them to a Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) outlet for real-time acquisition, synchronization, and visualization in experiments.

The Binder MK 53 is a laboratory climate chamber used to hold samples under controlled temperature conditions for incubation, conditioning, and stability testing. It supports temperature setpoint control and monitoring, and provides basic status information such as door state and operating mode.

This is a laboratory climate chamber used to expose samples to a controlled chamber environment for temperature-related stability testing, environmental simulation, and routine incubation or storage experiments. Samples are loaded through the chamber door, and the device provides operating-mode and door-status information.

This is a laboratory microplate heater shaker that provides temperature control and shaking for plate-based samples. It is commonly used for sample incubation, reaction mixing, enzymatic workflows, and nucleic acid or protein-related assays that require stable heating and continuous agitation. Some models also support plate locking and active cooling.

This is a laboratory thermoshaker for processing microplate samples. It provides shaking for liquid mixing and temperature control, and is commonly used for incubation, enzymatic reactions, and sample preparation workflows.

The Cytation is a microplate reader with integrated microscopy-style imaging. It can autofocus, move across wells, perform brightfield or filtered imaging, and control camera exposure, gain, objectives, and illumination. It is commonly used for imaging cell culture plates, fluorescence or brightfield observation, and automated data collection in plate-based assays.

This is a 96-well microplate absorbance reader used to measure sample absorbance in plate wells at selected wavelengths. It is suitable for ELISA, colorimetric assays, and other routine microplate-based laboratory measurements.

A superconducting transmon qubit controlled and measured with microwave pulses, a readout resonator, and flux pulses, using CBox-based electronics for timing and acquisition. It is used in quantum computing experiments for spectroscopy, Rabi, T1, Ramsey, echo, single-shot readout, randomized benchmarking, and characterization of flux pulses and CZ-related phase behavior.

The CLARIOstar is a multimode microplate reader used to measure absorbance, fluorescence, and luminescence in microplate samples. It is commonly used for biochemical assays, cell-based experiments, drug screening, and other high-throughput laboratory workflows.

A non-physical software component for shaker workflows. It provides interfaces for shaking, stopping, and plate locking/unlocking, mainly for testing, debugging, or simulating shaker behavior when no specific hardware is attached.

records.name_en: Cytomat Automated Microplate Incubator Storage System
records.description_en: This is an automated laboratory incubator and storage system for microplates, with internal storage positions, a transfer station, and an external exposed position. It can control temperature, CO2, humidity, and O2, and supports shaking and barcode reading. It is commonly used for cell culture, high-throughput screening, and automated plate management workflows.

records.name_en: Gatan TEM Camera and Energy Filter System
records.description_en: This is a Gatan imaging and energy-filter system for transmission electron microscopy. It can manage one or more microscope cameras and supports K2-class direct electron detector configuration, image acquisition, frame saving, and energy filter adjustment. It is commonly used in TEM and cryo-EM experiments for image recording, dose-fractionated acquisition, and zero-loss peak alignment.

A control box for Hamilton microplate heater-shaker units, used to heat and shake plates, lock or release plates, and read temperature information. It is commonly used for plate incubation, mixing, and automated laboratory workflows.

A laboratory device for heating and shaking microplates, with controllable temperature, start/stop shaking, and plate locking for stable operation. It is commonly used for sample incubation, reaction mixing, and on-deck plate processing in automated liquid handling workflows.

An automated microplate incubator and storage unit for laboratory automation workflows. It provides temperature control, shaking, and a transfer/loading station to move plates between internal racks and external handlers. It is used for microplate incubation, storage, and robotic high-throughput laboratory workflows.

This is a laboratory heater-shaker used to heat and shake sample plates and similar labware for mixing. It supports setting shaking speed and motion pattern, and some operations include plate locking/unlocking, making it suitable for incubation, mixing, and temperature-controlled sample handling.

A microplate incubator-shaker module with heating, temperature control, planar shaking, and a drawer-based loading mechanism. It is used as an individual unit in a stacked system for sample incubation, mixing, and temperature-controlled processing.

A stackable laboratory incubator shaker for temperature-controlled incubation and shaking of microplates and similar sample carriers. It includes a loading drawer or tray, temperature regulation, and two-axis shaking, and is used for cell culture, sample incubation, reaction mixing, and plate-based workflows in automated lab systems.

A laboratory automation device composed of multiple stackable incubator/shaker units with loading trays, used to provide temperature-controlled incubation and shaking for samples or microplates in automated culture, reaction incubation, and sample-processing workflows.

A multimode microplate reader used to measure signals from samples in microplates. It supports absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, fluorescence polarization, and time-resolved fluorescence measurements. The instrument is commonly used for biochemical assays, cell-based experiments, immunoassays, enzyme activity measurements, and high-throughput screening, with support for temperature control and plate shaking.

This is a controller and control-electronics unit used in scanning probe microscopy experiments, commonly paired with STM and AFM platforms. It connects the host computer to the microscope system and is used for experiment control, scan coordination, and measurement data exchange in automated laboratory microscopy workflows.

An OBF file used to store experimental data stacks and their metadata, commonly for microscopy and similar laboratory imaging workflows. It can contain multiple data stacks along with header information, descriptions, and unit-related metadata for storage, archiving, and offline analysis.

records.name_en: OpenBCI biosignal acquisition board with LSL streaming
records.description_en: Used to initialize and control an OpenBCI biosignal acquisition board and publish multichannel data through Lab Streaming Layer (LSL). The evidence shows serial board initialization, default channel configuration, daisy-module handling, start/stop acquisition, and channel location metadata management, making it suitable for EEG and related biosignal experiments with real-time streaming.

This is a multi-channel open-source biosensing board mainly used to acquire EEG signals, with additional auxiliary input channels. It can expand channel count with a daisy module and is commonly used for brain-computer interface experiments, neural signal recording, teaching, and general physiological signal acquisition.

An automated thermocycler module for PCR and related nucleic acid amplification workflows, providing programmed temperature cycling (denaturation, annealing, extension) with an opening heated lid for plate-based sample temperature control in automated lab protocols.

A laboratory thermocycler for PCR amplification, featuring a precisely controlled sample block and a heated lid. It performs denaturation, annealing, and extension temperature cycles on PCR plates and is suited for automated molecular biology workflows.

A benchtop thermocycler module for PCR and other thermal cycling workflows, featuring an openable heated lid and a temperature-controlled sample block. It runs programmed multi-step temperature profiles for DNA amplification, enzymatic incubations, and molecular biology sample heating.

The Opentrons Temperature Module is a temperature-control accessory for laboratory automation platforms. It heats or cools microplates or other small lab containers and maintains a set temperature for sample incubation, reagent cooling, and other temperature-sensitive workflows.
A PCR thermal cycler used for temperature cycling experiments. It can report temperature and run status, control heated-lid open/close and lid force, and manage, run, and delete onboard programs.

The Prior ProScan III is a microscope system controller that can connect to and control multiple filter wheels. It is commonly used in fluorescence microscopy and multichannel imaging to switch filter positions, select imaging channels, and coordinate microscope accessories.

records.name_en: Prior ProScan III Microscope Accessory Controller
records.description_en: A physical controller for microscope systems that manages accessories connected to the ProScan III; based on the available evidence, this mainly includes up to three filter wheel connections. It is used in laboratory microscopy setups to coordinate communication with attached accessories and to discover managed devices.
A thermocycler for PCR workflows that controls block and heated-lid temperatures, runs or aborts amplification protocols, and reports run status, steps, timing, and log information.

A drawer-based laboratory environmental control unit for incubating or storing samples or microplates under controlled conditions. It supports temperature control and can report liquid level, temperature, CO2 flow, valve status, and drawer status.

An automated incubator for culturing and storing microplates, with control of temperature, humidity, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen atmosphere. It supports plate loading and unloading through left/right cassettes or storage levels, and is commonly used in cell culture, live-cell assays, and automated biological workflows.

records.name_en: Tecan Freedom EVO automated liquid handling workstation
records.description_en: A benchtop automated liquid handling workstation for laboratory pipetting and plate movement. It typically includes a multichannel LiHa liquid handling arm for aspirating, dispensing, liquid level detection, disposable tip handling, and multi-axis positioning, and may work with 96-channel or plate-handling modules for sample preparation, microplate filling, and high-throughput workflows.

This is an automated liquid handling workstation used for laboratory pipetting and sample processing. The instrument arranges carriers, microplates, reagent troughs, cuvettes, magnetic modules, and disposable tip racks on a deck, and performs aspiration, dispensing, tip changes, and waste handling for tasks such as sample preparation, reagent distribution, and PCR setup.

A USB ultrasound probe used for ultrasound imaging. It is controlled through USB control and bulk transfers for initialization, register configuration, image acquisition, freeze/unfreeze operation, raw image retrieval, and Doppler-related acquisition, making it suitable for experimental ultrasound observation and data capture.

A climate chamber for laboratory environmental stress and temperature-control testing. It can read and set chamber temperature and control manual mode, condensation protection, compressed air, and air drying functions.

Controls and reads temperature, humidity, and digital channel states of a Weiss SB 22 climate chamber. The device communicates via RS-232 serial interface and is used for environmental simulation, sample aging, and temperature/humidity stability testing.

A non-physical control component for managing a set of daisy-chained Zaber devices over a serial connection. It exposes child devices such as stages, filter wheels, and LED controllers for microscopy and laboratory automation workflows.

records.name_en: Zaber daisy-chained motorized stage and optical peripheral system
records.description_en: This is a family of Zaber laboratory automation devices connected over a serial daisy chain, including motorized stages, filter wheels or filter cube turrets, and LED light controllers. It is commonly used in microscopy and optical experiments for automated sample positioning, filter switching, and illumination control.

This is a dual-beam microscope that combines a scanning electron microscope with a focused ion beam on one platform. It is used for surface imaging, ion-beam milling and patterning, gas-assisted deposition, precise stage positioning, and automated alignment. Typical lab uses include cross-section preparation, lamella preparation, trench milling, serial sectioning, and volume imaging workflows.

An instrument used to read absorbance, fluorescence, and luminescence signals from wells in a microplate, commonly used for biochemical assays, cell-based experiments, and plate-based analytical workflows.

The Olympus IX2 is an inverted microscope body used in laboratories to support the objective turret, illumination, and focusing mechanisms for microscopic sample observation. It is commonly used for cell culture work, live-sample observation, fluorescence imaging, and general biological microscopy involving Z-axis focusing and microscope body status control.

An automated laboratory centrifuge for sample separation, supporting rotor positioning, door open/close control, door and bucket locking, and spin programs based on target relative centrifugal force or RPM.
A laboratory device used to shake and mix sample plates. It can run at a specified speed for a set duration or continuously, and supports locking/unlocking the plate to keep it secure during shaking.

A laboratory centrifuge uses centrifugal force to separate components in liquid samples. It is commonly used for pelleting, phase separation, and sample preparation. This device supports door control, indexed bucket positions, and timed spin cycles at a specified g-force, making it suitable for automated sample-handling workflows.

This is a non-physical software control component that defines the basic control interface for a laboratory sealer, including sealing, temperature setting, and temperature readback, for use by higher-level workflows or concrete hardware implementations.
A laboratory automation device for sealing microplates. It supports sealing, opening and closing the mechanism, and setting or reading the temperature.

A laboratory device used to automatically remove sealing films or adhesive seals from microplates. It is commonly used in sample-processing and automated workflows to open plates before pipetting, plate reading, or analysis.

A data source used to store, read, and organize multidimensional microscopy image data and its metadata. It manages information such as voxel size, XYCZT dimensions, timepoints, channels, and z planes, and is commonly used for storing and accessing experimental imaging datasets.

A wafer prober used for semiconductor wafer electrical testing. It precisely positions the wafer and probe needles so instruments can contact and measure on-wafer devices, commonly for device characterization, process development, and failure analysis.

Used to communicate with Pylontech energy storage battery modules or their battery management interface, scan battery modules on the bus, and read protocol version, manufacturer information, system parameters, management information, serial numbers, and operating values for laboratory energy storage monitoring and integration.

A generic thermocycler for PCR and other thermal cycling workflows. It supports block and heated-lid temperature control, lid open/close operations, execution of multi-stage temperature protocols, and queries of current temperature, cycle progress, and run status.

A non-physical abstract software component for thermocyclers. It defines a unified control interface for opening and closing the lid, setting block and lid temperatures, deactivating heating, running thermocycling protocols, and reading temperatures, lid state, and protocol progress, to be implemented by concrete thermocycler devices.

This is a non-physical camera software component that provides a common abstraction for camera objects in microscopy acquisition and supports features such as camera mapping and multiview imaging. The evidence supports it being an abstract base/helper module for camera control rather than a specific camera instrument.

An automated laboratory incubator for storing and temperature-controlling microplates or assay plates. It typically provides multiple plate sites, a loading tray, and a door mechanism, allowing incubation at a set temperature as well as automated plate transfer and shaking. It is commonly used for cell culture, enzyme reactions, sample holding, and plate incubation steps in lab automation workflows.

An instrument interface for a Thermo Fisher focused ion beam scanning electron microscope (FIB-SEM). It supports electron/ion beam imaging, autofocus and autocontrast, beam shift, stage and nanomanipulator motion, ion-beam milling, GIS gas injection, and sputter/deposition-related operations for sample characterization, cross-section preparation, and micromanipulation workflows.

A non-physical software proxy that connects to an electron microscope through a remote microscope server. It is used to read TEM/STEM status, adjust beam, image, magnification, and operating modes, manage camera and detector parameters, and trigger image or signal acquisition.

This is a high-vacuum electron microscope that operates in transmission electron microscopy and scanning transmission electron microscopy modes for high-resolution imaging, electron diffraction, and related detection of specimens. The instrument typically includes an electron column with vacuum system, stage, viewing screen, cameras, and STEM detectors, and allows control of beam deflection, spot size, convergence angle, magnification, focus, and stigmation for materials, nanostructure, and thin-sample analysis.

A generic Bluetooth sensor or acquisition device that continuously sends measurement data to a lab computer and publishes it as an LSL stream for synchronized recording, online monitoring, and multimodal experiments. It is suitable for acquiring biosignals, motion signals, or other real-time sensor data.

A superconducting qubit used in low-temperature quantum measurement systems. It is controlled and read out with microwave signals and can be tuned with magnetic flux bias near sweet spots or anti-sweet spots. It is commonly used for continuous-wave spectroscopy, time-domain coherence experiments, flux tuning, automated characterization, and optimization of the qubit readout chain.
